name: Abdellatif Laâbi
representative_works: The Bottom of the Jar; Beyond the Hand
rationale: A long poetic and autobiographical career joins linguistic invention with imprisonment and exile.
main_reservation: The bilingual oeuvre requires broader reading than its limited English reception.

name: Adélia Prado
representative_works: The Alphabet in the Park; Ex-Voto
rationale: A distinctive lyric joins ordinary domestic life with embodied spirituality and desire.
main_reservation: A current status check and wider Portuguese reading are needed beyond English selections.

name: Adonis
representative_works: Songs of Mihyar the Damascene; A Time Between Ashes and Roses
rationale: Remade Arabic poetic language through myth, fragmentation and a sustained dialogue with inherited forms.
main_reservation: The case rests chiefly on poetry and requires close assessment across translations.

name: Alain Mabanckou
representative_works: Broken Glass; Memoirs of a Porcupine
rationale: Oral energy, satire and unconventional narration recast postcolonial and diasporic experience.
main_reservation: A final argument should weigh sustained achievement beyond exuberant narrative voice.

name: Alexis Wright
representative_works: Carpentaria; The Swan Book
rationale: Large, polyphonic narratives remake the novel through Indigenous sovereignty, oral forms and ecological time.
main_reservation: The culturally specific formal system requires informed reading rather than thematic shorthand.

name: Ali Smith
representative_works: How to Be Both; Autumn
rationale: Playful structures and narrative voices respond to art, time and contemporary social fracture.
main_reservation: The committee should test the durability of work closely tied to current events.

name: Alice Walker
representative_works: The Color Purple; Meridian
rationale: A multigenre oeuvre reshaped the representation of Black women’s interior lives and collective struggle.
main_reservation: Assessment needs to consider the wider career beyond the dominant landmark novel.

name: Amitav Ghosh
representative_works: The Glass Palace; Sea of Poppies
rationale: Historical novels and essays connect empire, migration and ecological crisis across the Indian Ocean.
main_reservation: The full literary case should distinguish fictional achievement from influential commentary.

name: Ananda Devi
representative_works: Eve Out of Her Ruins; Indian Tango
rationale: Intense narrative voices explore violence, caste, gender and marginal lives in Mauritius and beyond.
main_reservation: An assessment should establish sustained formal range beyond the best-known novels.

name: Anne Carson
representative_works: Autobiography of Red; Nox
rationale: Hybrid works remake the boundaries between classical scholarship, lyric, narrative and visual form.
main_reservation: The experimental corpus resists conventional comparisons of genre and scale.

name: Antjie Krog
representative_works: Country of My Skull; Lady Anne
rationale: Poetry and literary witness test the language of guilt, reconciliation and belonging.
main_reservation: The English nonfiction should not eclipse the Afrikaans poetry in evaluation.

name: Antonio Muñoz Molina
representative_works: Sepharad; In the Night of Time
rationale: Layered narratives join memory, exile and historical catastrophe through precise prose.
main_reservation: A final case needs to encompass the range beyond historical fiction.

name: Arnon Grunberg
representative_works: Tirza; The Jewish Messiah
rationale: Darkly comic novels probe humiliation, displacement and the fragility of moral identity.
main_reservation: English reception remains incomplete across a prolific career.

name: Arundhati Roy
representative_works: The God of Small Things; The Ministry of Utmost Happiness
rationale: Inventive syntax and layered narrative connect intimate damage with caste, state power and history.
main_reservation: A relatively small novel corpus leaves a case partly dependent on literary nonfiction.

name: Atiq Rahimi
representative_works: Earth and Ashes; The Patience Stone
rationale: Spare, concentrated narratives connect war, silence and gendered power.
main_reservation: The literary corpus is comparatively compact and overlaps with a film career.

name: Bae Suah
representative_works: Untold Night and Day; A Greater Music
rationale: Dislocated voices and temporal loops push Korean fiction toward musical and philosophical abstraction.
main_reservation: International translation covers a relatively small portion of the career.

name: Bakhtiyar Ali
representative_works: The Last Pomegranate Tree; I Stared at the Night of the City
rationale: Expansive, allegorical novels reimagine Kurdish history, violence and collective memory.
main_reservation: Limited translation remains a major barrier to fair comparative reading.

name: Bảo Ninh
representative_works: The Sorrow of War; Hà Nội at Midnight
rationale: Fragmented memory and lyrical narration unsettle heroic accounts of war.
main_reservation: The international case depends heavily on one novel; the stories need fuller reading.

name: Bei Dao
representative_works: The August Sleepwalker; City Gate, Open Up
rationale: Compressed, oblique poetry transformed the language of modern Chinese lyric and exile.
main_reservation: The wider achievement should not be reduced to political symbolism.

name: Ben Okri
representative_works: The Famished Road; Astonishing the Gods
rationale: Visionary fiction makes spirit worlds and material deprivation coexist in an original narrative register.
main_reservation: The committee would need to weigh the whole career beyond the breakthrough novel.

name: Bernardine Evaristo
representative_works: Girl, Woman, Other; The Emperor’s Babe
rationale: Hybrid verse and polyphonic fiction expand the representation of Black British lives.
main_reservation: The comparison needs to extend beyond the recent breakthrough in international recognition.

name: Bernardo Atxaga
representative_works: Obabakoak; The Accordionist’s Son
rationale: Inventive storytelling connects Basque language, communal memory and political violence.
main_reservation: Self-translation and varying editions complicate identification of the representative corpus.

name: Botho Strauß
representative_works: Big and Small; The Young Man
rationale: Fragmented dramatic and prose forms explore estrangement and the collapse of shared social languages.
main_reservation: Political commentary should be evaluated separately from the formal literary achievement.

name: Boubacar Boris Diop
representative_works: Murambi: The Book of Bones; Doomi Golo
rationale: Historical witness and writing in Wolof challenge both political violence and linguistic hierarchy.
main_reservation: The strongest comparison needs access to the Wolof as well as French work.

name: Can Xue
representative_works: Frontier; Love in the New Millennium
rationale: Dreamlike narrative worlds destabilize ordinary psychology, space and causal storytelling.
main_reservation: The surrealist methods require sustained reading beyond a few translated works.

name: Carmen Boullosa
representative_works: They’re Cows, We’re Pigs; Before
rationale: Inventive historical and fantastical narratives recast colonial power and women’s experience.
main_reservation: English translation provides an incomplete view of a very broad oeuvre.

name: Caryl Churchill
representative_works: Top Girls; Far Away
rationale: Radical theatrical forms reconfigure time, identity and political argument on stage.
main_reservation: Drama needs assessment through performance as well as translated scripts.

name: César Aira
representative_works: An Episode in the Life of a Landscape Painter; The Literary Conference
rationale: A prolific sequence of short novels makes improvisation and abrupt transformation into a distinctive literary method.
main_reservation: The huge, uneven corpus complicates any representative selection.

name: Charles Wright
representative_works: Black Zodiac; The World of the Ten Thousand Things
rationale: A sustained meditative poetry joins landscape, memory and metaphysical questioning.
main_reservation: The case needs to establish international significance beyond domestic honors.

name: Chico Buarque
representative_works: Budapest; Spilt Milk
rationale: Unreliable narrative voices and lyrical work explore class, desire and historical self-deception.
main_reservation: The award case should state how fiction, theatre and song lyrics contribute to the literary oeuvre.

name: Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie
representative_works: Half of a Yellow Sun; Americanah
rationale: Historical and diasporic novels render race, migration and social power through intimate lives.
main_reservation: A shorter career than many contenders leaves the lifetime-achievement comparison open.

name: Christoph Ransmayr
representative_works: The Last World; The Terrors of Ice and Darkness
rationale: Mythic and documentary narrative combine to explore catastrophe, exploration and human limits.
main_reservation: The committee should compare the wider oeuvre beyond the two early landmark novels.

name: Claudio Magris
representative_works: Danube; Microcosms
rationale: Hybrid travel, essay and fiction map Europe through borderlands, memory and intellectual history.
main_reservation: The achievement crosses genres and needs an explicit literary rather than scholarly comparison.

name: Colm Tóibín
representative_works: The Master; Brooklyn
rationale: Restrained narration makes exile, family and unspoken feeling central to historical and contemporary fiction.
main_reservation: A final case should specify formal achievement beyond thematic consistency.

name: Colson Whitehead
representative_works: The Underground Railroad; The Nickel Boys
rationale: Historical reinvention and genre experimentation illuminate American institutions and racial violence.
main_reservation: The lifetime-achievement comparison remains open against longer-established writers.

name: Conceição Evaristo
representative_works: Ponciá Vicêncio; Olhos d’Água
rationale: Interlinked memory and voice give Black Brazilian women’s experiences a distinctive literary form.
main_reservation: The committee should establish formal achievement across works beyond their social importance.

name: Cristina Peri Rossi
representative_works: The Ship of Fools; State of Exile
rationale: A multigenre oeuvre joins exile, desire and political displacement through inventive narrative and lyric forms.
main_reservation: The poetry and stories need as much attention as the best-known novel.

name: Cristina Rivera Garza
representative_works: No One Will See Me Cry; Liliana’s Invincible Summer
rationale: Experimental fiction and archival writing question authorship, violence and the recovery of erased lives.
main_reservation: The comparative case should encompass the fiction alongside recent acclaimed nonfiction.

name: Dacia Maraini
representative_works: The Silent Duchess; Bagheria
rationale: A long multigenre oeuvre examines women’s lives, silence and historical power.
main_reservation: The committee should assess the entire career beyond its most familiar novels.

name: David Malouf
representative_works: Remembering Babylon; Ransom
rationale: Lyrical fiction and poetry explore encounters between cultures, bodily experience and historical memory.
main_reservation: The full poetry and short fiction should be weighed alongside the novels.

name: Diamela Eltit
representative_works: E. Luminata; The Fourth World
rationale: Radical narrative structures connect bodily experience with dictatorship and social exclusion.
main_reservation: A demanding, partially translated corpus makes comparative reading difficult.

name: Dionne Brand
representative_works: A Map to the Door of No Return; Ossuaries
rationale: Poetry and essay unsettle the languages of diaspora, slavery and belonging.
main_reservation: The formally demanding corpus has less international exposure than some peers.

name: Don DeLillo
representative_works: White Noise; Underworld
rationale: A distinctive prose examines media, technology, mass culture and historical consciousness.
main_reservation: The committee would need to assess the later work alongside the canonical middle period.

name: Drago Jančar
representative_works: I Saw Her That Night; The Galley Slave
rationale: Shifting perspectives and historical fiction explore coercion, memory and human agency.
main_reservation: International comparison requires more than the most widely translated historical novel.

name: Duo Duo
representative_works: Words as Movement; The Boy Who Catches Wasps
rationale: A highly individual modernist lyric transforms historical rupture into dense verbal music.
main_reservation: Translation remains a substantial obstacle to comparison of the poetic texture.

name: Dương Thu Hương
representative_works: Paradise of the Blind; Novel Without a Name
rationale: Fiction confronts war, disillusionment and moral survival through intimate narrative voices.
main_reservation: Political visibility must be weighed separately from sustained literary achievement.

name: Durs Grünbein
representative_works: Ashes for Breakfast; The Vocation of Poetry
rationale: A major poetic project connects bodily perception, classical inheritance and modern German history.
main_reservation: A fair assessment requires sustained reading of German poetic form.

name: Eduardo Mendoza
representative_works: The Truth About the Savolta Case; The City of Marvels
rationale: Historical reconstruction and comic experiment recast the social novel of modern Spain.
main_reservation: The committee would need to weigh formal range across serious and comic work.

name: Edward P. Jones
representative_works: The Known World; All Aunt Hagar’s Children
rationale: Layered narration gives Black communities and the history of slavery unusual moral complexity.
main_reservation: The small published corpus is the principal comparative limitation.

name: Edwidge Danticat
representative_works: The Farming of Bones; Brother, I’m Dying
rationale: Fiction and memoir make Haitian history and migration legible through intimate, interlinked lives.
main_reservation: A citation should distinguish narrative achievement from the importance of its subject.

name: Eka Kurniawan
representative_works: Beauty Is a Wound; Man Tiger
rationale: Myth, grotesque humor and historical violence meet in formally energetic Indonesian fiction.
main_reservation: The internationally visible corpus remains smaller than that of many veteran contenders.

name: Elena Ferrante
representative_works: My Brilliant Friend; The Days of Abandonment
rationale: A sustained investigation of women’s friendship, class and selfhood reworks social narrative.
main_reservation: The public identity is unverified; practical award arrangements would require private resolution.

name: Elena Poniatowska
representative_works: Massacre in Mexico; Here’s to You, Jesusa!
rationale: Documentary polyphony gives marginalized lives a powerful place in Mexican literary history.
main_reservation: The ethical mediation of others’ testimony deserves direct assessment.

name: Elif Shafak
representative_works: The Bastard of Istanbul; 10 Minutes 38 Seconds in This Strange World
rationale: Polyphonic novels connect gender, cultural inheritance and migration across languages.
main_reservation: Wide readership needs to be matched by a precise account of formal innovation.

name: Emmanuel Carrère
representative_works: The Adversary; The Kingdom
rationale: Self-implicating documentary narratives explore belief, violence and the ethics of telling other lives.
main_reservation: The committee would need to evaluate the ethical and formal limits of the narrator’s self-insertion.

name: Enrique Vila-Matas
representative_works: Bartleby & Co.; Dublinesque
rationale: Metafiction turns the literary life, quotation and failed authorship into inventive narrative engines.
main_reservation: The self-referential aesthetic may appear narrower than more socially expansive alternatives.

name: Erri De Luca
representative_works: God’s Mountain; The Day Before Happiness
rationale: Compressed prose brings labor, spiritual inheritance and historical experience into intimate narrative.
main_reservation: The restrained scale of individual works calls for evaluation across the full corpus.

name: Ewa Lipska
representative_works: A New Century; Dear Ms. Schubert
rationale: Ironic, compressed poetry tests the language of social conformity, memory and modern estrangement.
main_reservation: Translation offers an incomplete view of a long poetic career.

name: Geetanjali Shree
representative_works: Tomb of Sand; The Empty Space
rationale: Playful, expansive Hindi prose unsettles borders of language, gender and historical memory.
main_reservation: International assessment should extend beyond the single breakthrough translation.

name: George Saunders
representative_works: Tenth of December; Lincoln in the Bardo
rationale: Inventive voices and speculative situations turn moral pressure into new short-story and novel forms.
main_reservation: The comparatively recent novel-length work leaves a chiefly short-fiction case.

name: Gerald Murnane
representative_works: The Plains; Border Districts
rationale: A radically inward fiction builds distinctive systems of landscape, memory and mental images.
main_reservation: Its deliberately narrow aesthetic world may divide comparative judgments.

name: Ghassan Zaqtan
representative_works: Like a Straw Bird It Follows Me; Describing the Past
rationale: A restrained poetics of traces and absence transforms Palestinian memory into oblique lyric form.
main_reservation: International visibility remains narrower than that of several prose contenders.

name: Gioconda Belli
representative_works: The Inhabited Woman; The Country Under My Skin
rationale: A long multigenre oeuvre joins erotic autonomy, revolutionary history and women’s political experience.
main_reservation: The committee should distinguish formal achievement from public and political symbolism.

name: Goenawan Mohamad
representative_works: Selected Poems; Catatan Pinggir
rationale: Poetry and literary essays sustain a distinctive dialogue between freedom, history and cultural tradition.
main_reservation: A representative translated selection is needed to assess the large essay corpus.

name: Gonçalo M. Tavares
representative_works: Jerusalem; Learning to Pray in the Age of Technique
rationale: Interconnected fictional and philosophical projects examine systems, cruelty and modern rationality.
main_reservation: The large, heterogeneous corpus calls for a carefully justified representative selection.

name: Gonzalo Celorio
representative_works: And Let the Earth Tremble at Its Centers; Three Pretty Cubans
rationale: Urban narrative and family memory join intimate histories with Mexican and Caribbean cultural experience.
main_reservation: International translation and reception are relatively limited.

name: Hanan al-Shaykh
representative_works: The Story of Zahra; Women of Sand and Myrrh
rationale: Women’s voices expose the intimate workings of war, migration and social constraint.
main_reservation: The committee would need to distinguish the literary case from thematic importance alone.

name: Haruki Murakami
representative_works: The Wind-Up Bird Chronicle; Kafka on the Shore
rationale: Recurring dream worlds and estranged narrators reshaped the international reach of Japanese fiction.
main_reservation: Global popularity does not settle debates over repetition and unevenness.

name: Hélène Cixous
representative_works: The Book of Promethea; The Third Body
rationale: Experimental writing dissolves boundaries between autobiography, philosophy and fiction.
main_reservation: Her theoretical influence should be separated from the literary achievement itself.

name: Hélia Correia
representative_works: The Return of Lilias Fraser; Perdition
rationale: Mythic and theatrical writing connects women’s voices, history and literary inheritance.
main_reservation: Limited translation makes genre breadth difficult to compare internationally.

name: Hiromi Kawakami
representative_works: Strange Weather in Tokyo; The Nakano Thrift Shop
rationale: Understated and fantastical narratives expose oddness within everyday relations.
main_reservation: The comparative case needs to encompass the more experimental work.

name: Hoda Barakat
representative_works: The Stone of Laughter; The Night Mail
rationale: Unstable voices and fractured communities turn displacement into a distinctive narrative form.
main_reservation: A relatively compact translated corpus makes breadth harder to compare.

name: Homero Aridjis
representative_works: Solar Poems; 1492: The Life and Times of Juan Cabezón of Castile
rationale: Poetry and historical fiction connect ecological imagination, myth and the lives displaced by history.
main_reservation: Environmental prominence should be separated from the sustained literary case.

name: Hwang Sok-yong
representative_works: The Guest; Mater 2-10
rationale: A long fictional career recovers divided histories through layered voices and social worlds.
main_reservation: The literary argument should be distinguished from biography and political courage.

name: Ian McEwan
representative_works: Atonement; Saturday
rationale: Precise narrative structures expose the moral consequences of misreading, desire and historical contingency.
main_reservation: The committee would need to distinguish sustained innovation from literary prestige.

name: Ibrahim al-Koni
representative_works: Gold Dust; The Bleeding of the Stone
rationale: A desert cosmology joins Tuareg experience, ecological limits and metaphysical fiction.
main_reservation: The symbolic system can be difficult to assess through a small translated sample.

name: Ibrahim Nasrallah
representative_works: Time of White Horses; The Second War of the Dog
rationale: A large narrative project reconstructs Palestinian history alongside speculative and lyrical writing.
main_reservation: The strongest case needs to establish the formal achievement across the wider oeuvre.

name: Ida Vitale
representative_works: Pre-texts; Byobu
rationale: Exacting lyric and prose miniatures explore language, perception and the intellectual life of exile.
main_reservation: Age warrants a current status check; translation conveys only part of the poetic texture.

name: Ivan Vladislavić
representative_works: The Restless Supermarket; Portrait with Keys
rationale: Fragmented urban narratives make language and the built environment register historical change.
main_reservation: International recognition is less extensive than the achievement merits; close reading is essential.

name: Jamaica Kincaid
representative_works: Annie John; A Small Place
rationale: A sharp narrative voice links colonial power, family intimacy and landscape.
main_reservation: A relatively concentrated oeuvre requires attention to its range across genres.

name: Jaume Cabré
representative_works: Confessions; Voices of the Pamano
rationale: Polyphonic novels connect individual guilt, music and the long afterlife of European violence.
main_reservation: The case requires assessment beyond the two most visible translated novels.

name: Javier Cercas
representative_works: Soldiers of Salamis; The Anatomy of a Moment
rationale: Investigative narratives unsettle the boundary between documented history and imaginative reconstruction.
main_reservation: The case should distinguish his formal contribution from the importance of Spanish historical debates.

name: Jeanette Winterson
representative_works: Oranges Are Not the Only Fruit; Written on the Body
rationale: Innovative narratives unsettle inherited categories of gender, sexuality and selfhood.
main_reservation: The career’s range and uneven critical reception call for a selective but fair reading.

name: Jenny Erpenbeck
representative_works: Visitation; Kairos
rationale: Compressed structures connect intimate relations with state histories and the consequences of political change.
main_reservation: The case should extend beyond recent international prize recognition.

name: Jessica Hagedorn
representative_works: Dogeaters; The Gangster of Love
rationale: Collage and popular-culture voices connect dictatorship, migration and diasporic identity.
main_reservation: The case requires evaluation across fiction, performance and poetry.

name: Jeyamohan
representative_works: Vishnupuram; The White Elephant
rationale: Philosophical and historical fiction builds a large, ambitious Tamil narrative world.
main_reservation: Limited translation makes comparative evaluation unusually difficult.

name: John Banville
representative_works: The Book of Evidence; The Sea
rationale: Highly worked prose and unreliable narrators turn memory and aesthetic perception into moral problems.
main_reservation: Stylistic brilliance needs to be weighed against the range of the wider oeuvre.

name: John Edgar Wideman
representative_works: Philadelphia Fire; Brothers and Keepers
rationale: Experimental narration connects family history, incarceration and the public record of race.
main_reservation: The dispersed, formally demanding oeuvre has a less unified international reception.

name: Jón Kalman Stefánsson
representative_works: Heaven and Hell; Your Absence Is Darkness
rationale: Lyrical, intergenerational narratives connect harsh environments with love, loss and communal memory.
main_reservation: The translated novels should be tested for range beyond a recognizable lyrical register.

name: Jorie Graham
representative_works: The Dream of the Unified Field; Sea Change
rationale: Syntax and perception become instruments for confronting time, embodiment and ecological crisis.
main_reservation: Her demanding poetics divide readers and depend heavily on close reading.

name: Joy Harjo
representative_works: She Had Some Horses; An American Sunrise
rationale: Poetry joins Muscogee memory, music and survivance in a distinctive contemporary voice.
main_reservation: Institutional prominence should be separated from a close assessment of poetic innovation.

name: Joyce Carol Oates
representative_works: them; Blonde
rationale: An exceptionally large oeuvre maps violence, class and gender through varied narrative forms.
main_reservation: The scale and unevenness of the corpus make selection of representative work consequential.

name: Julian Barnes
representative_works: Flaubert’s Parrot; The Sense of an Ending
rationale: Playful structures and unreliable memory connect literary history with ordinary ethical failure.
main_reservation: The case rests on subtle tonal and structural achievements rather than a single defining innovation.

name: K. Satchidanandan
representative_works: While I Write; Misplaced Objects and Other Poems
rationale: A long poetic career joins modernist experimentation with ethical and multilingual engagement.
main_reservation: Translation and a dispersed bibliography complicate a representative assessment.

name: Karl Ove Knausgaard
representative_works: My Struggle; The Morning Star
rationale: A sustained autobiographical project reconfigured the scale and texture of ordinary-life narration.
main_reservation: Self-exposure and volume do not by themselves establish literary innovation.

name: Kerstin Ekman
representative_works: Blackwater; The Forest of Hours
rationale: A large novelistic oeuvre joins women’s histories, landscape and ecological time with narrative invention.
main_reservation: Former Swedish Academy membership requires explicit consideration in a simulation of Academy preferences.

name: Kim Hyesoon
representative_works: Autobiography of Death; Phantom Pain Wings
rationale: Radical bodily and spectral imagery reworks lyric voice through feminist and collective experience.
main_reservation: The case depends on assessing poetic innovation through several translations.

name: Ko Un
representative_works: Ten Thousand Lives; Flowers of a Moment
rationale: A vast poetic project joins individual lives with Korea’s historical experience.
main_reservation: Public misconduct allegations are a reputational consideration; the literary corpus also needs selective assessment.

name: László Végel
representative_works: Memoirs of a Pimp; Neoplanta
rationale: A borderland oeuvre interrogates minority life, urban memory and historical displacement.
main_reservation: Limited international translation makes the broader achievement harder to assess.

name: Latife Tekin
representative_works: Dear Shameless Death; Berji Kristin: Tales from the Garbage Hills
rationale: Oral forms and collective voices transform rural migration and urban dispossession into narrative invention.
main_reservation: The English corpus represents only part of a sustained career.

name: Laura Restrepo
representative_works: Delirium; The Dark Bride
rationale: Layered narrative voices connect political violence with intimate and psychological disorder.
main_reservation: The case needs a comparative account of formal range across the oeuvre.

name: Leila Aboulela
representative_works: The Translator; Minaret
rationale: Interior narratives of migration and faith broaden the moral vocabulary of the English novel.
main_reservation: The case requires a clear account of formal distinctiveness across the oeuvre.

name: Leonardo Padura
representative_works: The Man Who Loved Dogs; Heretics
rationale: Crime and historical narratives use investigative structures to examine disillusionment and displaced memory.
main_reservation: A literary case must encompass the work beyond the prestige of historical subjects.

name: Li Ang
representative_works: The Butcher’s Wife; The Lost Garden
rationale: Feminist fiction confronts sexual power and Taiwan’s social and political history.
main_reservation: International translation coverage is uneven across the career.

name: Lídia Jorge
representative_works: The Murmuring Coast; The Wind Whistling in the Cranes
rationale: A sustained novelistic oeuvre interrogates colonial memory, gender and changing Portuguese society.
main_reservation: The wider corpus is only unevenly represented in English.

name: Louise Erdrich
representative_works: Love Medicine; The Night Watchman
rationale: Interlinked Indigenous narratives join communal memory, legal power and inventive storytelling.
main_reservation: The full multivolume project needs evaluation beyond its recent prize-winning books.

name: Ludmila Petrushevskaya
representative_works: The Time: Night; There Once Lived a Woman Who Tried to Kill Her Neighbor’s Baby
rationale: Dark fables, dramatic voices and compressed narratives expose the violence of ordinary domestic life.
main_reservation: The international case needs both dramatic and prose corpora.

name: Ludmila Ulitskaya
representative_works: The Big Green Tent; Daniel Stein, Interpreter
rationale: Interwoven lives explore dissent, spiritual pluralism and the moral experience of Soviet history.
main_reservation: The comparative case should distinguish narrative achievement from political reputation.

name: Luis Mateo Díez
representative_works: The Fountain of Age; The Ruin of Heaven
rationale: A large imagined provincial world joins oral storytelling with grotesque and dreamlike fiction.
main_reservation: Limited English availability makes international comparison harder.

name: Luisa Valenzuela
representative_works: The Lizard’s Tail; He Who Searches
rationale: Experimental fiction exposes the relation between political terror, sexuality and narrative authority.
main_reservation: International circulation covers only part of a long career.

name: Lutz Seiler
representative_works: Kruso; Star 111
rationale: Poetry and fiction render East German memory through dense attention to voice and material life.
main_reservation: The international translated corpus is still relatively narrow.

name: Lydia Davis
representative_works: The Collected Stories of Lydia Davis; Can’t and Won’t
rationale: Extreme compression and linguistic precision expanded what a short story can do.
main_reservation: The miniature form requires comparison without equating length with achievement.

name: Mahmoud Dowlatabadi
representative_works: Kelidar; The Colonel
rationale: Large social narratives and concentrated tragic fiction explore rural change and political violence.
main_reservation: Much of the foundational Persian oeuvre is not readily available in English.

name: Margaret Atwood
representative_works: The Handmaid’s Tale; Alias Grace
rationale: A large, versatile oeuvre examines gender, power and ecological danger through narrative invention.
main_reservation: Public prominence should not substitute for comparing the full literary achievement.

name: Margo Glantz
representative_works: The Family Tree; The Wake
rationale: Fragmented autobiographical and critical writing joins migration, the body and cultural memory.
main_reservation: A dispersed, cross-genre oeuvre makes representative reading difficult.

name: Maria Stepanova
representative_works: In Memory of Memory; Holy Winter 20/21
rationale: Poetry and hybrid historical writing investigate archival absence and the ethics of remembrance.
main_reservation: The international case should include the poetry rather than rely chiefly on one prose book.

name: Marie NDiaye
representative_works: Three Strong Women; My Heart Hemmed In
rationale: Uncanny narrative voices expose exclusion, family power and unstable belonging.
main_reservation: The translated sample remains incomplete across fiction and theatre.

name: Marilynne Robinson
representative_works: Housekeeping; Gilead
rationale: Meditative prose and moral interiority bring theology, family and American history into dialogue.
main_reservation: The small number of novels makes the breadth of the achievement a comparative question.

name: Mathias Énard
representative_works: Zone; Compass
rationale: Formally ambitious narratives connect Mediterranean histories, violence and cultural entanglement.
main_reservation: The strongest comparison should test the wider oeuvre beyond two major landmarks.

name: Maxine Hong Kingston
representative_works: The Woman Warrior; China Men
rationale: Hybrid autobiography and myth transformed the representation of migration and inherited stories.
main_reservation: Genre boundaries and a concentrated core corpus require a precise literary case.

name: Mei-mei Berssenbrugge
representative_works: Empathy; A Treatise on Stars
rationale: Long-line experimental poetry explores perception, relation and the boundaries of the human.
main_reservation: The specialized poetic reception makes a broader comparative case necessary.

name: Mia Couto
representative_works: Sleepwalking Land; Confession of the Lioness
rationale: Linguistic invention brings oral storytelling into novels of war, memory and postcolonial life.
main_reservation: Wordplay and oral registers are particularly sensitive to translation.

name: Michael Ondaatje
representative_works: The English Patient; Anil’s Ghost
rationale: Lyrical fragmentation connects private lives with war, migration and unstable historical records.
main_reservation: The case must balance the poetry with the more widely known fiction.

name: Michel Houellebecq
representative_works: The Elementary Particles; The Map and the Territory
rationale: Satirical novels diagnose commodified intimacy and social exhaustion through a distinctive narrative voice.
main_reservation: Provocation and public notoriety should not substitute for literary comparison.

name: Mikhail Shishkin
representative_works: Maidenhair; The Light and the Dark
rationale: Layered voices and temporal structures connect mortality, language and historical survival.
main_reservation: A relatively small novel corpus makes the scale comparison significant.

name: Milton Hatoum
representative_works: The Brothers; Tale of a Certain Orient
rationale: Layered family narratives connect Amazonian spaces, migration and the instability of memory.
main_reservation: The internationally visible corpus remains relatively compact.

name: Minae Mizumura
representative_works: A True Novel; The Fall of Language in the Age of English
rationale: Formal reinvention of the Japanese novel connects literary inheritance with linguistic inequality.
main_reservation: The compact corpus makes the scale of the lifetime achievement a question.

name: Mircea Cărtărescu
representative_works: Blinding; Solenoid
rationale: Visionary, densely patterned prose turns memory and the body into an expansive metaphysical project.
main_reservation: The scale and translation demands make selective reading a significant risk.

name: Mohsin Hamid
representative_works: The Reluctant Fundamentalist; Exit West
rationale: Compact, formally inventive novels connect migration, global power and unstable identity.
main_reservation: A relatively small corpus leaves the lifetime-achievement comparison open.

name: Nona Fernández
representative_works: The Twilight Zone; Space Invaders
rationale: Fragmented narratives connect intimate memory with the erased lives of dictatorship.
main_reservation: International recognition rests on a relatively small translated portion of the oeuvre.

name: Nuruddin Farah
representative_works: Maps; Secrets
rationale: A long sequence of novels interrogates state power, kinship and exile through shifting perspectives.
main_reservation: A final case should identify the most distinctive formal achievement within a very broad oeuvre.

name: Oksana Zabuzhko
representative_works: Fieldwork in Ukrainian Sex; The Museum of Abandoned Secrets
rationale: Feminist and historical narratives join bodily experience with suppressed cultural memory.
main_reservation: Translation gives only partial access to a substantial multigenre oeuvre.

name: Olvido García Valdés
representative_works: And We Were All Alive; The Dream of the Body
rationale: An elliptical poetry probes perception, bodily vulnerability and the relation between language and being.
main_reservation: Translation is limited and the poetic texture resists brief summaries.

name: Oya Baydar
representative_works: The Lost Word; The General of the Garbage Dump
rationale: Fiction explores memory, ideological failure and social fragmentation through changing perspectives.
main_reservation: International recognition and translation are less extensive than the domestic oeuvre.

name: Pascal Quignard
representative_works: All the World’s Mornings; The Roving Shadows
rationale: Fragmentary writing links music, memory and ancient texts in an unusually coherent cross-genre project.
main_reservation: The dispersal and learned texture of the oeuvre complicate representative reading.

name: Pat Barker
representative_works: Regeneration; The Silence of the Girls
rationale: Historical fiction scrutinizes war, trauma and the voices excluded from heroic narratives.
main_reservation: The literary case should identify the formal contribution beyond historical recovery.

name: Patricia Grace
representative_works: Potiki; Cousins
rationale: Māori communal voices and narrative structures challenge dominant accounts of land and identity.
main_reservation: The translated and international reception is narrower than the local significance.

name: Patrick Chamoiseau
representative_works: Texaco; Slave Old Man
rationale: Creolized narrative forms bring oral memory and collective history into the modern novel.
main_reservation: Language-specific innovation requires informed evaluation across translations.

name: Paul Muldoon
representative_works: Moy Sand and Gravel; Meeting the British
rationale: Virtuosic rhyme and associative structures join historical violence with linguistic play.
main_reservation: Formal ingenuity and emotional force require careful comparison across collections.

name: Per Petterson
representative_works: Out Stealing Horses; I Curse the River of Time
rationale: Restrained narration turns family estrangement and rural memory into concentrated emotional structures.
main_reservation: A relatively consistent aesthetic needs comparison for range as well as precision.

name: Percival Everett
representative_works: Erasure; The Trees
rationale: Genre shifts, satire and philosophical play expose the structures of racial representation.
main_reservation: Recent visibility should be weighed against the breadth of a much longer career.

name: Perumal Murugan
representative_works: One Part Woman; Poonachi
rationale: Rural voices and fable examine caste, sexuality and the coercion of ordinary life.
main_reservation: The case requires a broader Tamil corpus assessment beyond internationally prominent titles.

name: Peter Carey
representative_works: Oscar and Lucinda; True History of the Kelly Gang
rationale: Inventive voices rework colonial history and the myths of Australian identity.
main_reservation: The committee needs to weigh the later oeuvre against the established landmark novels.

name: Péter Nádas
representative_works: A Book of Memories; Parallel Stories
rationale: Complex structures of perception and embodiment connect private lives with European history.
main_reservation: The large, demanding corpus requires unusually substantial comparative reading.

name: Pia Tafdrup
representative_works: Queen’s Gate; Tarkovsky’s Horses
rationale: A sustained lyric project makes embodiment, perception and historical memory formally interdependent.
main_reservation: The international translated selection remains limited.

name: Piedad Bonnett
representative_works: What Has No Name; The Wretches
rationale: Poetry and autobiographical prose connect grief, mental illness and ordinary social violence.
main_reservation: The internationally visible nonfiction should not eclipse the poetry.

name: Pierre Michon
representative_works: Small Lives; The Eleven
rationale: Dense, compressed prose transforms obscure lives and art history into powerful narrative inquiry.
main_reservation: A small core corpus raises questions of scale without diminishing literary intensity.

name: Pirkko Saisio
representative_works: The Red Book of Farewells; Lowest Common Multiple
rationale: Experimental autobiography and drama connect queer identity, class and Finland’s social transformations.
main_reservation: Limited translation complicates evaluation across a substantial multigenre career.

name: Raduan Nassar
representative_works: Ancient Tillage; A Cup of Rage
rationale: Intense rhythmic prose transforms family, desire and authority within a small but influential corpus.
main_reservation: The exceptionally small oeuvre makes breadth the clearest comparative question.

name: Raúl Zurita
representative_works: Purgatory; Anteparadise
rationale: Large poetic sequences and landscape-scale interventions transform suffering into collective memorial form.
main_reservation: Performance and visual dimensions require assessment beyond printed translation.

name: Reina María Rodríguez
representative_works: The Winter Garden; The Varieties of the Real World
rationale: An intimate, materially attentive lyric transforms scarcity, memory and urban experience.
main_reservation: Limited translation and a specialized reception make the comparison demanding.

name: Richard Powers
representative_works: The Gold Bug Variations; The Overstory
rationale: Formally ambitious novels connect scientific systems with emotional and ecological life.
main_reservation: The balance between conceptual exposition and fictional force merits scrutiny.

name: Rita Dove
representative_works: Thomas and Beulah; Sonata Mulattica
rationale: Poetic sequences connect intimate lives with the historical erasure of Black experience.
main_reservation: The committee would need to assess formal range across the complete poetry.

name: Rohinton Mistry
representative_works: A Fine Balance; Family Matters
rationale: Socially expansive novels render ordinary lives under political pressure with moral complexity.
main_reservation: The limited number of published books makes sustained range a comparative question.

name: Ryszard Krynicki
representative_works: Our Life Is Growing; Magnetic Point
rationale: A movement toward poetic compression connects linguistic vigilance with historical and ethical pressure.
main_reservation: The small-scale, exacting lyric requires assessment in and across the original language.

name: Sahar Khalifeh
representative_works: Wild Thorns; The Inheritance
rationale: A sustained Palestinian feminist oeuvre connects national struggle with class and domestic power.
main_reservation: Translation coverage is uneven across a substantial career.

name: Salman Rushdie
representative_works: Midnight’s Children; The Satanic Verses
rationale: Verbal abundance and hybrid histories transformed the postcolonial novel’s narrative possibilities.
main_reservation: Political symbolism should not displace evaluation of a varied and uneven oeuvre.

name: Samanta Schweblin
representative_works: Fever Dream; Little Eyes
rationale: Compressed, unsettling narratives give technological and ecological anxiety unusual formal precision.
main_reservation: A comparatively short career leaves the lifetime-achievement question open.

name: Scholastique Mukasonga
representative_works: Our Lady of the Nile; The Barefoot Woman
rationale: Fiction and memorial prose recover social worlds destroyed by the Rwandan genocide.
main_reservation: The case must articulate literary innovation as well as the force of testimony.

name: Sebastian Barry
representative_works: The Secret Scripture; Days Without End
rationale: Musical voices recover lives obscured by Irish and transatlantic history.
main_reservation: The comparison should encompass drama and poetry as well as the best-known novels.

name: Selina Hossain
representative_works: Hangor Nodi Grenade; Gayatri Sandhya
rationale: A large Bengali oeuvre connects liberation history with women’s lives and social change.
main_reservation: Restricted international translation makes the formal comparison difficult.

name: Seno Gumira Ajidarma
representative_works: Eyewitness; Jazz, Perfume and the Incident
rationale: Experimental storytelling and documentary fragments confront repression and the instability of evidence.
main_reservation: Translation coverage is limited and complicates evaluation of the wider oeuvre.

name: Sergio Ramírez
representative_works: Margarita, How Beautiful the Sea; Divine Punishment
rationale: Historical and civic narratives combine irony, documentary detail and the social worlds of Central America.
main_reservation: Political stature should be weighed separately from the novelistic achievement.

name: Serhiy Zhadan
representative_works: Voroshilovgrad; The Orphanage
rationale: Poetry and fiction transform postindustrial lives and wartime dislocation through distinctive voices.
main_reservation: Current visibility should be weighed against the full prewar literary career.

name: Shahrnush Parsipur
representative_works: Women Without Men; Touba and the Meaning of Night
rationale: Mythic and experimental narratives recast women’s historical and spiritual experience.
main_reservation: Translation offers a limited view of the broader oeuvre.

name: Sjón
representative_works: The Blue Fox; Moonstone
rationale: Compressed, mythic narratives connect folklore, queer lives and historical violence.
main_reservation: The poetry and wider Icelandic corpus require assessment alongside translated novellas.

name: Slavenka Drakulić
representative_works: S.: A Novel About the Balkans; The Taste of a Man
rationale: Fiction and literary essays examine bodily vulnerability, war and ordinary complicity.
main_reservation: The balance between fiction and public commentary needs a precise literary case.

name: Stefan Hertmans
representative_works: War and Turpentine; The Convert
rationale: Hybrid historical narratives connect intimate records with the larger pressures of European history.
main_reservation: The poetry and earlier prose should not be eclipsed by recent translated novels.

name: Su Tong
representative_works: Raise the Red Lantern; The Boat to Redemption
rationale: Atmospheric prose examines desire, patriarchy and historical rupture through tightly controlled worlds.
main_reservation: English reception covers only part of a much larger oeuvre.

name: Susan Howe
representative_works: My Emily Dickinson; That This
rationale: Archival fragments and visual arrangements remake relations between history and poetic voice.
main_reservation: Page design and linguistic texture complicate translation and comparative evaluation.

name: Sylvie Germain
representative_works: The Book of Nights; The Weeping Woman on the Streets of Prague
rationale: Mythic and lyrical fiction turns historical violence into a sustained inquiry into suffering and memory.
main_reservation: International recognition does not cover the full breadth of the career.

name: Tahar Ben Jelloun
representative_works: The Sand Child; This Blinding Absence of Light
rationale: Gendered storytelling and narratives of incarceration examine the instability of social identity.
main_reservation: The unevenness of a prolific oeuvre should be assessed directly.

name: Thomas Pynchon
representative_works: Gravity’s Rainbow; Mason & Dixon
rationale: Encyclopedic fiction links systems of power, scientific knowledge and countercultural imagination.
main_reservation: Density and uneven accessibility complicate comparative reading across the whole oeuvre.

name: Tim Winton
representative_works: Cloudstreet; Breath
rationale: Vernacular prose connects class, coastal environments and spiritual longing.
main_reservation: A strong regional achievement still needs a persuasive international comparison.

name: Tsitsi Dangarembga
representative_works: Nervous Conditions; This Mournable Body
rationale: A connected novel sequence traces the psychic costs of colonialism, gender and class.
main_reservation: The concentrated fictional corpus offers less genre breadth than some alternatives.

name: Tua Forsström
representative_works: Snow Leopard; After Having Spent a Night Among Horses
rationale: Concentrated lyric and associative sequences connect grief, nature and the instability of perception.
main_reservation: Former Swedish Academy membership and limited translation require explicit contextual review.

name: Véronique Tadjo
representative_works: The Shadow of Imana; In the Company of Men
rationale: Polyphonic narrative and fable connect collective memory, violence and ecological interdependence.
main_reservation: A multilingual reading of the wider oeuvre would strengthen the comparison.

name: Vikram Seth
representative_works: A Suitable Boy; The Golden Gate
rationale: Large social narrative and technically inventive verse fiction join classical forms with modern lives.
main_reservation: The major works are few and widely spaced, making the breadth comparison consequential.

name: Vladimir Sorokin
representative_works: Day of the Oprichnik; Blue Lard
rationale: Radical stylistic imitation and grotesque speculation expose the literary machinery of authoritarian power.
main_reservation: Shock and provocation need to be assessed for their formal necessity.

name: Wang Anyi
representative_works: The Song of Everlasting Sorrow; Fu Ping
rationale: Detailed urban narratives give changing social worlds and women’s lives historical depth.
main_reservation: A fuller translated sample is needed to compare the range of the oeuvre.

name: William T. Vollmann
representative_works: Europe Central; Rising Up and Rising Down
rationale: Large narrative and documentary projects investigate violence, ethics and marginal experience.
main_reservation: The enormous, uneven corpus is difficult to assess comprehensively.

name: Witi Ihimaera
representative_works: The Whale Rider; Bulibasha
rationale: A substantial Māori oeuvre brings genealogy, community and cultural change into modern fiction.
main_reservation: The committee should establish literary range beyond the best-known adapted novel.

name: Yan Lianke
representative_works: The Four Books; The Explosion Chronicles
rationale: Grotesque and mythic narrative forms expose the violence of ideology and development.
main_reservation: The comparison should assess formal invention independently of censorship and political visibility.

name: Yang Lian
representative_works: Narrative Poem; Concentric Circles
rationale: Long poetic structures join cultural memory, exile and formal experimentation.
main_reservation: The demanding architecture calls for more than a brief anthology-based assessment.

name: Yoko Ogawa
representative_works: The Memory Police; The Housekeeper and the Professor
rationale: Quietly unsettling narratives investigate memory, bodily vulnerability and control.
main_reservation: The extensive Japanese corpus is only partly represented in English.

name: Yoko Tawada
representative_works: The Emissary; Memoirs of a Polar Bear
rationale: Bilingual writing turns linguistic estrangement into inventive narrative and poetic forms.
main_reservation: Both language corpora need evaluation; one translated novel is insufficient.

name: Yu Hua
representative_works: To Live; Brothers
rationale: A changing narrative style brings ordinary survival into contact with extreme historical violence.
main_reservation: The contrast between restrained early work and broad later satire merits evaluation.

name: Yuri Andrukhovych
representative_works: Perverzion; Moscoviad
rationale: Carnivalesque prose and poetry challenged Soviet narrative conventions and remade Ukrainian urban imagination.
main_reservation: Political urgency should not replace assessment of the long-standing formal achievement.

name: Yusef Komunyakaa
representative_works: Dien Cai Dau; Neon Vernacular
rationale: Musical language and sensory precision transform war and racial history into sustained lyric achievement.
main_reservation: An international comparison requires attention to a primarily American reception.

name: Zoë Wicomb
representative_works: You Can’t Get Lost in Cape Town; David’s Story
rationale: Fragmented narrative dismantles racial classification and inherited accounts of resistance.
main_reservation: The formally complex, relatively small corpus calls for careful comparative reading.
